chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar who said:
I asked him (peace be upon him) about praying in a Jurmuq (gaiter/large slipper), and I brought a Jurmuq to him and sent it to him, so he said: 'One may pray in it.'

key_terms.جُرْمُوقٍ: A large slipper or gaiter worn on the foot

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray while wearing large slippers or gaiters (Jurmuq)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar inquires of Imam al-Rida (or the relevant Imam depending on the specific chain's attribution in broader contexts, though often cited in discussions of clothing validity) regarding the *Jurmuq*, a large leather slipper or gaiter. The Imam’s affirmative response clarifies that this specific type of footwear does not constitute a defect in clothing that would invalidate the prayer, distinguishing it from garments that are too loose or transparent. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh for establishing the boundaries of valid attire, emphasizing that practicality and coverage are prioritized over strict uniformity, provided the garment meets the basic requirements of *awrah* coverage.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ibrahim Bin Mahziyar who said,
‘I asked himasws about the Salāt in a Jurmuq (gaiter – a large slipper), and I came with a gaiter and showed it to himasws. So heasws said: ‘One can pray Salāt in it’.
en.sarwar: 32. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar who has said the following: “

I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a Jurmuq (a larger slipper worn over another one) if it is permissible to perform Salah (prayer) with it and I showed it to him (the Imam) and he (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible to perform Salah (prayer) with it.’”
